_comment: DED-1881 fixture. Every other test_payer in_network file (ours and the CMS examples) publishes `npi` as a JSON NUMBER, so the whole smoke corpus was ONE publisher shape and could not see a type defect. UnitedHealthcare publishes `npi` as a JSON STRING; aetna, anthem and cigna publish numbers. On production image baa2e47 the NPI filter compared an int set against the parsed value with a bare `in`, so every UHC NPI-scoped pull returned ZERO rows, SUCCEEDED, silently. This file is the string half of the corpus. NPI 3333333333 is the NPI the 7-job e2e suite already filters on (job3), and TIN 99-9991881 appears ONLY here -- so job3's rows must CONTAIN that TIN (string shape matched) and must NOT contain NPI 9999999991 (the reduce still drops non-matching NPIs from the same array). Both comparison sites are exercised: the MS-DRG object resolves through top-level provider_references, the CPT object through inline provider_groups.
